It reduces costs and boosts efficiency with prompt compression, improving RAG performance by up to 21.4% using only 1/4 of the tokens.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.91/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eLongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression\u003c/a\u003e (ACL 2024 and ICLR ME-FoMo 2024)\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003cem\u003eHuiqiang Jiang, Qianhui Wu, Xufang Luo, Dongsheng Li, Chin-Yew Lin, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLLMLingua-2, a small-size yet powerful prompt compression method trained via data distillation from GPT-4 for token classification with a BERT-level encoder, excels in task-agnostic compression. It surpasses LLMLingua in handling out-of-domain data, offering 3x-6x faster performance.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.57/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eLLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression\u003c/a\u003e (ACL 2024 Findings)\u003cbr\u003e\n\u003cem\u003eZhuoshi Pan, Qianhui Wu, Huiqiang Jiang, Menglin Xia, Xufang Luo, Jue Zhang, Qingwei Lin, Victor Ruhle, Yuqing Yang, Chin-Yew Lin, H. \u003cstrong\u003eLLMLingua-2\u003c/strong\u003e!\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThese tools offer an efficient solution to compress prompts by up to \u003cstrong\u003e20x\u003c/strong\u003e, enhancing the utility of LLMs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e💰 \u003cstrong\u003eCost Savings\u003c/strong\u003e: Reduces both prompt and generation lengths with minimal overhead.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e📝 \u003cstrong\u003eExtended Context Support\u003c/strong\u003e: Enhances support for longer contexts, mitigates the \"lost in the middle\" issue, and boosts overall performance.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e⚖️ \u003cstrong\u003eRobustness\u003c/strong\u003e: No additional training needed for LLMs.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e🕵️ \u003cstrong\u003eKnowledge Retention\u003c/strong\u003e: Maintains original prompt information like ICL and reasoning.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e📜 \u003cstrong\u003eKV-Cache Compression\u003c/strong\u003e: Accelerates inference process.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e🪃 \u003cstrong\u003eComprehensive Recovery\u003c/strong\u003e: GPT-4 can recover <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">TL;DR</h2><a id="user-content-tldr" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: TL;DR" href="#tldr"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">LLMLingua utilizes a compact, well-trained language model (e.g., GPT2-small, LLaMA-7B) to identify and remove non-essential tokens in prompts. This approach enables efficient inference with large language models (LLMs), achieving up to 20x compression with minimal performance loss.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.825/" rel="nofollow">LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models</a> (EMNLP 2023)<br>
<em>Huiqiang Jiang, Qianhui Wu, Chin-Yew Lin, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu</em></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">LongLLMLingua mitigates the 'lost in the middle' issue in LLMs, enhancing long-context information processing. It reduces costs and boosts efficiency with prompt compression, improving RAG performance by up to 21.4% using only 1/4 of the tokens.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.91/" rel="nofollow">LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression</a> (ACL 2024 and ICLR ME-FoMo 2024)<br>
<em>Huiqiang Jiang, Qianhui Wu, Xufang Luo, Dongsheng Li, Chin-Yew Lin, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu</em></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">LLMLingua-2, a small-size yet powerful prompt compression method trained via data distillation from GPT-4 for token classification with a BERT-level encoder, excels in task-agnostic compression. It surpasses LLMLingua in handling out-of-domain data, offering 3x-6x faster performance.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.57/" rel="nofollow">LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression</a> (ACL 2024 Findings)<br>
<em>Zhuoshi Pan, Qianhui Wu, Huiqiang Jiang, Menglin Xia, Xufang Luo, Jue Zhang, Qingwei Lin, Victor Ruhle, Yuqing Yang, Chin-Yew Lin, H. Vicky Zhao, Lili Qiu, Dongmei Zhang</em></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">SecurityLingua is a safety guardrail model that uses the security-aware prompt compression to reveal the malicious intentions behind jailbreak attacks, enabling LLMs to detect attacks and generate safe responses. Due to the highly efficient prompt compression, the defense involves negligible overhead and 100x less token costs compared to state-of-the-art LLM guardrail approaches.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="https://openreview.net/forum?id=tybbSo6wba" rel="nofollow">SecurityLingua: Efficient Defense of LLM Jailbreak Attacks via Security-Aware Prompt Compression</a> (CoLM 2025)<br>
<em>Yucheng Li, Surin Ahn, Huiqiang Jiang, Amir H. Abdi, Yuqing Yang and Lili Qiu</em></li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/microsoft/LLMLingua/blob/main/images/LLMLingua_motivation.png"><img src="/microsoft/LLMLingua/raw/main/images/LLMLingua_motivation.png" alt="Background" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Ever encountered the token limit when asking ChatGPT to summarize lengthy texts?</li>
<li>Frustrated with ChatGPT forgetting previous instructions after extensive fine-tuning?</li>
<li>Experienced high costs using GPT3.5/4 API for experiments despite excellent results?</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">While Large Language Models like ChatGPT and GPT-4 excel in generalization and reasoning, they often face challenges like prompt length limits and prompt-based pricing schemes.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/microsoft/LLMLingua/blob/main/images/motivation.png"><img src="/microsoft/LLMLingua/raw/main/images/motivation.png" alt="Motivation for LLMLingua" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Now you can use <strong>LLMLingua</strong>, <strong>LongLLMLingua</strong>, and <strong>LLMLingua-2</strong>!</p>
<p dir="auto">These tools offer an efficient solution to compress prompts by up to <strong>20x</strong>, enhancing the utility of LLMs.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>💰 <strong>Cost Savings</strong>: Reduces both prompt and generation lengths with minimal overhead.</li>
<li>📝 <strong>Extended Context Support</strong>: Enhances support for longer contexts, mitigates the "lost in the middle" issue, and boosts overall performance.</li>
<li>⚖️ <strong>Robustness</strong>: No additional training needed for LLMs.</li>
<li>🕵️ <strong>Knowledge Retention</strong>: Maintains original prompt information like ICL and reasoning.</li>
<li>📜 <strong>KV-Cache Compression</strong>: Accelerates inference process.</li>
<li>🪃 <strong>Comprehensive Recovery</strong>: GPT-4 can recover all key information from compressed prompts.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">With <strong>LLMLingua</strong>, you can easily compress your prompts. Here’s how you can do it:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">llmlingua</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">PromptCompressor</span>

<span class="pl-s1">llm_lingua</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">PromptCompressor</span>()
<span class="pl-s1">compressed_prompt</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">llm_lingua</span>.<span class="pl-c1">compress_prompt</span>(<span class="pl-s1">prompt</span>, <span class="pl-s1">instruction</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">""</span>, <span class="pl-s1">question</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">""</span>, <span class="pl-s1">target_token</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">200</span>)

<span class="pl-c"># > {'compressed_prompt': 'Question: Sam bought a dozen boxes, each with 30 highlighter pens inside, for $10 each box. He reanged five of boxes into packages of sixlters each and sold them $3 per. He sold the rest theters separately at the of three pens $2. How much did make in total, dollars?\nLets think step step\nSam bought 1 boxes x00 oflters.\nHe bought 12 * 300ters in total\nSam then took 5 boxes 6ters0ters.\nHe sold these boxes for 5 *5\nAfterelling these  boxes there were 3030 highlighters remaining.\nThese form 330 / 3 = 110 groups of three pens.\nHe sold each of these groups for $2 each, so made 110 * 2 = $220 from them.\nIn total, then, he earned $220 + $15 = $235.\nSince his original cost was $120, he earned $235 - $120 = $115 in profit.\nThe answer is 115',</span>
<span class="pl-c">#  'origin_tokens': 2365,</span>
<span class="pl-c">#  'compressed_tokens': 211,</span>
<span class="pl-c">#  'ratio': '11.2x',</span>
<span class="pl-c">#  'saving': ', Saving $0.1 in GPT-4.'}</span>

<span class="pl-c">## Or use the phi-2 model,</span>
<span class="pl-s1">llm_lingua</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">PromptCompressor</span>(<span class="pl-s">"microsoft/phi-2"</span>)

<span class="pl-c">## Or use the quantation model, like TheBloke/Llama-2-7b-Chat-GPTQ, only need <8GB GPU memory.</span>
